summary: In this excerpt from Book 6, the narrator and Arthur question Sonya Halliday after learning that her colleague Katie stole the proof Halliday hired them to recover. Halliday, shaken, sits against a tree, and the group debates where Katie might have fled, considering her lack of family, possible NSA or DHS involvement, and whether a financial or professional motive explains the theft. Halliday describes Katie's strong career, including two recently accepted papers, and admits to some envy. The narrator suggests Katie may have stolen those papers too, and Arthur offers that they may have been bought, while the narrator notes the proof's world-changing significance as a possible motive.
one_line: Halliday's colleague Katie is revealed as the thief of the stolen proof, and the group tries to work out where she has gone and why.
key_facts: Arthur tells the narrator to stop talking and tries to comfort Sonya Halliday, who sits down against a tree on wet ground.
Halliday says the family Katie has left is all back on the reservation in New Mexico.
Halliday says Katie's parents are gone and there is no one left she is close to.
Arthur suggests an Indian reservation might be outside NSA jurisdiction and a good place for Katie to run.
The narrator says the NSA's jurisdiction is wherever the NSA says it is, and that the DHS and a secret black ops branch are similar.
Halliday says that in 2013, after waiting in line for hours, Katie finally saw the original 'Impression, Sunrise' painting up close.
Halliday says Katie had tenure, as both of them did, and had just gotten two groundbreaking papers accepted for publication.
Halliday confesses to some envy because the last two papers were not in Katie's field and Katie had no collaborators.
The narrator suggests Katie stole both of those papers too, and Halliday objects that the authors would have come forward.
Arthur suggests Katie may have bought the two papers, and says there could be plenty of reasons the authors never came forward.
The narrator says Halliday's proof was going to change the world and would have made her go down in history, which some people would steal for.
Halliday says Katie burned the proof, and the narrator argues Katie has her own copy and does not want anyone else touching it.
